Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q2 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Jane Smith, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech’s Q2 earnings call. Joining me today are Mark Johnson, CEO; Lisa Williams, CFO; and David Lee, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations site. Today’s discussion may include forward-looking statements. With that, let me turn the call over to Mark Johnson.

Mark Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Jane, and welcome everyone.

We’re pleased with our performance this quarter. I want to highlight a few areas:

Our gross profit increased sequentially by KRW 0.5 trillion, reaching KRW 21.1 trillion in Q3, up from KRW 20.6 trillion in Q2. This translates to a gross margin of 39.8%, a substantial 2.7 percentage point increase compared to the 37.1% we reported in the previous quarter. This improvement is primarily attributable to the successful execution of our cost optimization strategies, especially within our Memory division. Specifically, the accelerated process migration to our Gen5 architecture, particularly the shift from 1y nm to 1z nm DRAM and the ramp-up of 176-layer NAND, proved to be a key driver. We've seen a nearly 15% reduction in per-bit manufacturing costs associated with our Gen5 DRAM compared to the previous generation, largely due to improved yields and reduced material consumption. Furthermore, we saw improvements in our System LSI division, particularly in the mobile application processor (AP) segment. The yield improvements on our 4nm mobile APs, used in several flagship smartphones, contributed approximately KRW 0.1 trillion to the gross profit improvement. Finally, the remaining KRW 0.1 trillion came from improvements in the Foundry business, where we saw both increased capacity utilization and a better product mix, with a higher proportion of advanced nodes (5nm and below) contributing to the revenue.

Our total Capital Expenditure for the second quarter of 2024 reached KRW 9.8 trillion. This represents a slight decrease of 3% compared to Q1 2024, but a 7% increase compared to Q2 2023. This increase year-over-year is primarily driven by strategic investments in our Foundry business. The lion's share of our Q2 CapEx, KRW 8.6 trillion, was allocated to the Semiconductor division. The majority of the Memory investment focused on two key areas: process migration to our next-generation 1-alpha nanometer DRAM and 238-layer NAND flash memory technologies. Our Foundry investments were strategically channeled towards expanding capacity for both 5-nanometer and 8-nanometer process nodes. Our Display division received KRW 0.8 trillion in Q2. The focus here is on enhancing yields and improving the performance of our next-generation QD-OLED panels.

As we review our Q2 2024 performance, I want to start with an overview of Average Selling Prices (ASPs) across our wafer portfolio. Overall, we observed a positive ASP trend this quarter, driven primarily by continued strong demand and strategic pricing initiatives, particularly in the memory segments. The tightening supply chain, combined with robust demand from the data center, automotive, and mobile sectors, created a favorable pricing environment. We saw a blended wafer ASP increase of approximately 8% quarter-over-quarter. However, it's crucial to note that ASP increases are not uniform across all nodes and segments. While memory experienced significant gains, certain mature nodes within our foundry business faced price pressures due to increased competition and existing fab capacity globally.

I’ll now pass it over to Lisa Williams to walk through the numbers in more detail.

Lisa Williams, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Mark, and hello, everyone.

Let me break it down starting with overall wafer ASP comments, and the by node or segment wafer ASP comments for this quarter. As Mark mentioned, DRAM saw a substantial increase in ASP during Q2, rising by approximately 10%. The ASP for DDR5 wafers experienced the strongest growth, increasing by 12% Q/Q, while DDR4 ASP saw a more moderate increase of around 5% Q/Q. NAND Flash also exhibited positive ASP trends, with an overall increase of mid-single digits in Q2. 3D NAND drove the ASP increase. While QLC NAND offers the lowest cost per bit, its ASP saw a relatively modest increase of around 3% Q/Q. While memory drove the overall ASP increase, our foundry business presented a mixed picture. ASPs for advanced nodes remained relatively stable, with a slight increase of around 2% Q/Q, while mature nodes faced significant price pressure, with ASPs declining by an average of 3% Q/Q.

Now, moving to utilization rate, and the utilization rate guidance for the next quarter and future outlook, and any comments in the Q&A session, which we’ve been tracking closely. Our current DRAM utilization rate stands at approximately 87% across our major fabrication facilities. We anticipate our DRAM bit growth in Q3 to mirror the overall market, which we project to be flat. Specifically, we expect a DRAM bit growth of 0-2% for Q3. Looking beyond Q3, we expect the DRAM market to gradually recover in Q4, driven by a seasonal uptick in demand and the launch of new processor platforms. Our NAND utilization rate is currently at 95%, reflecting the stronger demand environment. We anticipate the overall NAND market to grow in the mid-single digits in Q3. More specifically, we project a 4-6% growth for the market as a whole. Importantly, we expect our NAND bit growth to exceed this market growth, fueled by strong demand for our enterprise SSDs and our expanding presence in the mobile NAND market. We're guiding for 8-10% NAND bit growth for Q3.

Lastly, I'd like to briefly touch on revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, revenue results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons. This has historically been more volatile, but our total revenue for the quarter landed at KRW 53 trillion. This represents a 4.3% decrease compared to Q1 2024 and a 5.6% decrease year-over-year. The 4.3% QoQ decline requires a nuanced explanation. We observed strength in our Memory division offset by headwinds in our SET business, primarily impacting our Mobile eXperience (MX) division. The Memory division demonstrated robust performance, achieving a 7.2% QoQ increase. The SET division experienced a significant contraction in Q2. We saw an 11.5% QoQ decline. The 5.6% YoY decline in total revenue reflects similar challenges but also highlights some strategic shifts and evolving market dynamics. Last quarter, our guidance projected total revenue of KRW 55 trillion for Q2 2024. The actual revenue of KRW 53 trillion represents a shortfall of approximately KRW 2 trillion, or 3.6%.

Now, let me hand things over to David Lee to talk about product and operational progress.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Lisa.

This was a busy quarter for our teams. On the innovation front, we made meaningful advances around Operating margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Operating margin results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons. StellarTech demonstrated a strong operating performance in Q3 2024, significantly exceeding expectations. The operating margin reached 15.4%, a notable improvement both sequentially and year-over-year. The 15.4% margin reflects a return to a healthier profitability level, demonstrating the resilience of StellarTech's diversified portfolio and the effectiveness of its strategic initiatives. Compared to Q2 2024, the operating profit increased by KRW 1.7 trillion, and the margin improved by 3.3 percentage points, driven primarily by the Memory Division Profitability Surge. The one-time gain in the Display business recorded a one-time gain of approximately KRW 400 billion related to the settlement of a long-standing contractual dispute with a major customer in the smartphone industry. The Consumer Electronics (CE) division, particularly the Home Appliance business, benefited from strong seasonality in Q3. Compared to Q3 2023, operating profit increased by KRW 800 billion, and the margin improved by 1.2 percentage points. The recovery in the Memory division was also a key driver of the YoY improvement, and the SET businesses implemented aggressive cost management initiatives throughout the year. The actual Q3 2024 operating margin of 15.4% outperformed the Q2 2024 Guidance for Q3 2024 Operating Margin of 13.5% - 14.5% due to Stronger-than-Expected Memory Recovery and the Unforeseen Display Business Gain.

Also worth noting is our improvement in gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Gross margin results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons. Comparing Q3 2024 to Q3 2023, we've observed a 3.5 percentage point increase in gross margin. This year, we've successfully navigated these challenges through strategic sourcing initiatives, including diversifying our supplier base and negotiating more favorable long-term contracts. In addition, the increased demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI accelerators and high-performance computing has also played a significant role. During our Q2 2024 earnings call, we guided for a gross margin in the range of 38.0% to 38.5% for Q3. Our actual gross margin of 39.8% significantly exceeded this guidance, primarily due to faster-than-expected ramp-up of Gen5 DRAM and higher ASP for NAND flash memory. Geographically, our gross margin performance was particularly strong in North America and Europe, driven by robust demand for data center solutions and high-end mobile devices.

And we’ve made foundational changes in how we approach CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this quarter, particularly on the fulfillment and logistics side. Our Semiconductor CapEx was allocated to Memory and Foundry. The majority of the Memory investment focused on process migration to our next-generation 1-alpha nanometer DRAM and 238-layer NAND flash memory technologies. Our Foundry investments were strategically channeled towards expanding capacity for both 5-nanometer and 8-nanometer process nodes. Our Display division received KRW 0.8 trillion in Q2, focused on enhancing yields and improving the performance of our next-generation QD-OLED panels. The cumulative CapEx for the first half of 2024 reached KRW 17.1 trillion, representing a 12% increase compared to the first half of 2023, underscoring our commitment to long-term growth and technological leadership. Looking ahead, we anticipate a slight moderation in CapEx spending in the second half of 2024 compared to the first half.

Let’s now open the floor for questions.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, revenue results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons, could you expand on what’s driving that strength?

Mark Johnson:
Certainly. While we saw a slight overall decline in revenue, the strength in our Memory division was a key positive. This was fueled by sustained demand from data centers, particularly for high-capacity DDR5 DRAM, driven by the ongoing AI boom. We also saw resilience in the PC market, supporting sales of our premium SSDs and DRAM. We're actively diversifying our supply chain and focusing on product innovation to mitigate the challenges in the SET division and capitalize on growth opportunities in the memory market.

Analyst 2:
A follow-up on utilization rate, and the utilization rate guidance for the next quarter and future outlook, and any comments in the Q&A session. How confident are you that you can maintain the projected NAND bit growth exceeding market growth, given the potential for increased competition?

Lisa Williams:
We are confident in our ability to outperform the market in NAND bit growth. This is based on our strong relationships with key cloud service providers, our competitive pricing on QLC NAND, and our expanding presence in the mobile NAND market. We are also seeing improved yields from our 176-layer NAND technology, which is contributing to improved cost efficiencies. We are closely monitoring the competitive landscape and are prepared to adjust our strategies as needed to maintain our market share.

Analyst 3:
And for Operating margin results, QoQ changes, YoY changes with reasons, Operating margin results  v.s. guidance from last quarter with reasons, any update on the sustainability of the Display business's one-time gain?

David Lee:
As you noted, the Display business did benefit from a one-time gain this quarter. While we don't anticipate a similar gain in the immediate future, we are focused on improving the underlying profitability of the division through innovation in QD-OLED technology, enhancing yields, and optimizing our product mix. We are also seeing strong demand from the premium TV segment, which is supporting higher margins.

Analyst 4:
Just a final one — on CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this quarter, is the improvement mostly from increased efficiency, or are there any specific projects being delayed?

Lisa Williams:
The moderation in CapEx spending in the second half of the year is primarily due to increased efficiency in our capital deployment and the completion of key equipment upgrades in the Display division. We are not delaying any strategically important projects. Our investments in advanced memory and foundry technologies remain a top priority. We are closely monitoring macroeconomic conditions and adjusting our investment plans accordingly, but we remain committed to our long-term growth objectives.

Closing

Mark Johnson:
Thank you again for joining us today. We remain confident in our long-term growth story and are committed to disciplined execution. We appreciate your continued interest and support.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
